learning_objective: 🎯 Discover the journey of a curious child! Learn how asking questions, collecting things, and parental support can create a world-class scientist.

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: प्यूपा (तितली के विकास की एक अवस्था)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Richard Ebright was an only child who loved collecting rocks, fossils, coins, and especially butterflies. By second grade, he had collected all 25 species of butterflies found near his hometown.
His mother was his biggest supporter. She bought him a book called 'The Travels of Monarch X', which opened the world of real science for him by inviting readers to tag butterflies for research.

In 7th grade, he entered a science fair with a simple slide display and lost. He realized real science isn't just showing things; it's doing real experiments. He started researching viral diseases in caterpillars.
Ebright discovered an unknown insect hormone from the gold spots on a Monarch pupa. This led to his groundbreaking theory on how cells 'read' their DNA, changing biology forever.
The chapter highlights three essential qualities: a first-rate mind, driving curiosity, and the will to win for the right reasons (not just for prizes, but to do the best job possible).

fun_activity.title: 🔍 Your Inner Scientist
fun_activity.instructions: Ebright started by collecting butterflies. What is something YOU like to collect or observe? (Leaves, stamps, coding bugs?). Write down one scientific question you have about your collection!

exam_tips: 📌 Highlight the role of Ebright's mother: She bought him equipment, took him on trips, and got him the crucial book.
📌 Explain the purpose of the 12 gold spots on a Monarch pupa (they produce a hormone necessary for butterfly development, not just for decoration).
📌 Memorize the 3 key ingredients in the 'making of a scientist' mentioned at the end.
quick_recap: ⭐ Dr. Urquhart from the University of Toronto guided Ebright through his butterfly research.
⭐ Ebright was not just a scientist; he was also a champion debater, public speaker, and photographer.
⭐ Winning is good, but wanting to do the best job possible is the true mark of genius.
